summary: Criminalizes knowingly and willfully making materially false, fictitious, or fraudulent statements or representations in any matter within the jurisdiction of the US government. Frequently charged in fraud and perjury-adjacent prosecutions.
key_text: paraphrase: whoever knowingly and willfully makes any materially false statement in a matter within the executive, legislative, or judicial branch jurisdiction is fined and/or imprisoned.
penalties: Fine and imprisonment up to 5 years.
applicability: Anyone making false statements to US government agencies (SEC, FTC, DOJ, etc.).

summary: Prohibits use of the postal system or interstate carriers to execute a scheme to defraud. A workhorse charge for fraud schemes involving mailed documents, including investor communications.
key_text: paraphrase: whoever devises a scheme to defraud and uses the mail to execute it is fined and/or imprisoned.
penalties: Fine and imprisonment up to 20 years.
applicability: Any scheme using US mail or commercial carriers in furtherance of fraud.

summary: Prohibits use of interstate wire, radio, or television communications to execute a scheme to defraud. Applied to fraudulent electronic communications, including AI-generated or automated outreach used in fraud.
key_text: paraphrase: whoever transmits by wire in interstate commerce a communication for the purpose of executing a scheme to defraud is fined and/or imprisoned.
penalties: Fine and imprisonment up to 20 years.
applicability: Any fraudulent scheme carried out over interstate wires, including the internet.

summary: Criminalizes schemes to defraud persons in connection with securities of covered issuers, or to obtain money or property by false statements in connection with the purchase or sale of such securities.
key_text: paraphrase: whoever knowingly executes a scheme to defraud in connection with any covered security is fined and/or imprisoned.
penalties: Fine and imprisonment up to 25 years.
applicability: Issuers, officers, and anyone making false statements in securities transactions (relevant to AI-company valuation claims).

summary: Criminalizes unauthorized access to computers, including access exceeding authorization, and the theft of information from protected computers. Central statute for data-scraping and unauthorized access disputes involving AI training data.
key_text: paraphrase: whoever intentionally accesses a computer without authorization or exceeds authorized access and obtains information is subject to criminal and civil liability.
penalties: Criminal fines and imprisonment up to 10 years for repeat/serious violations; civil damages available.
applicability: Anyone accessing protected computers without authorization; litigated extensively re: web scraping.

summary: Criminalizes retaliation against a person who provides truthful information to a federal law enforcement officer about the commission or possible commission of a federal offense. Creates federal criminal exposure for employers who retaliate against whistleblowers.
key_text: paraphrase: whoever knowingly engages in conduct intended to retaliate against a person for providing truthful information to federal law enforcement about a federal offense is fined and/or imprisoned.
penalties: Fine and imprisonment up to 20 years.
applicability: Employers and individuals who retaliate against persons who report federal crimes, including AI safety concerns that implicate federal law.

summary: Protects employees of publicly traded companies (and their contractors/subcontractors/agents) from retaliation for reporting conduct that they reasonably believe constitutes fraud against shareholders, mail/wire/securities fraud, or violations of SEC rules. Enforced administratively by OSHA/DOL with private right of action after 180 days.
key_text: paraphrase: no employer with securities registered under the Exchange Act may discharge or otherwise discriminate against an employee for providing information about conduct the employee reasonably believes violates federal securities laws or SEC rules.
penalties: Reinstatement, back pay, compensatory damages, and attorney fees.
applicability: Employees of publicly traded companies only — a documented blindspot for private/pre-IPO AI labs.

summary: Prohibits using income from a pattern of racketeering activity to acquire an interest in an enterprise, or conducting an enterprise's affairs through a pattern of racketeering. Enables civil RICO suits with treble damages.
key_text: paraphrase: it is unlawful to invest proceeds of racketeering in an enterprise, or to conduct an enterprise through a pattern of racketeering activity.
penalties: Criminal: up to 20 years per count; civil: treble damages, costs, and attorney fees.
applicability: Enterprises engaged in a pattern of predicate offenses (fraud, obstruction) — including corporate conduct involving systematic fraud.

summary: Prohibits unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce. The FTC's primary enforcement tool for AI products, from deceptive marketing claims to data practices. Does not require proof of intent.
key_text: paraphrase: unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce are declared unlawful.
penalties: Administrative orders, injunctions, civil penalties (up to statutory caps per violation), and consumer redress.
applicability: All persons and entities engaged in commerce, including AI vendors making capability or safety claims.

summary: Prohibits fraud in the offer or sale of securities, including making untrue statements of material fact or omitting material facts. Does not require proof that the purchaser relied on the misstatement.
key_text: paraphrase: it is unlawful to employ any device, scheme, or artifice to defraud, or to obtain money by means of untrue statements of material fact, in the offer or sale of securities.
penalties: SEC enforcement actions, disgorgement, penalties, and criminal prosecution.
applicability: Companies and persons offering or selling securities, including via public statements about AI capabilities.

summary: Prohibits fraud in connection with the purchase or sale of any security, including material misstatements or omissions. The primary private right of action for securities fraud, requiring scienter (intent to deceive).
key_text: paraphrase: it is unlawful to use any manipulative or deceptive device in connection with the purchase or sale of any security.
penalties: SEC enforcement, private class actions, disgorgement, and criminal prosecution.
applicability: Public companies and their executives making material statements — including AI revenue/capability claims — to investors.

summary: Establishes the SEC whistleblower bounty program: awards of 10-30% of monetary sanctions collected in SEC actions based on original, voluntary information. Includes anti-retaliation protection for whistleblowers who report to the SEC.
key_text: paraphrase: the SEC shall pay awards to whistleblowers who voluntarily provide original information leading to successful enforcement, and no employer may retaliate against such whistleblowers.
penalties: Bounties of 10-30% of sanctions; anti-retaliation remedies: reinstatement, back pay, double back pay, attorney fees.
applicability: Individuals reporting securities law violations to the SEC, including AI-related disclosure violations.

summary: Creates a civil cause of action for false or misleading descriptions of fact in commercial advertising or promotion that misrepresent the nature, characteristics, or qualities of goods or services. Used against exaggerated AI capability claims.
key_text: paraphrase: any person who uses a false or misleading description of fact in commercial advertising concerning goods or services is liable in a civil action.
penalties: Injunctions, defendant's profits, damages, costs, and attorney fees (no proof of intent required).
applicability: Competitors and consumers suing over false advertising of AI products and services.

summary: World's first comprehensive AI regulation. Risk-tiered framework: prohibited practices (e.g., social scoring, certain manipulation), high-risk system obligations (risk management, data governance, transparency, human oversight), general-purpose AI (GPAI) model obligations (documentation, copyright policy, systemic-risk duties), and transparency obligations for chatbots and deepfakes. Entered into force 1 August 2024; prohibitions applied from 2 February 2025; GPAI obligations from 2 August 2025; most high-risk obligations from 2 August 2026.
key_text: paraphrase: AI systems are classified by risk; prohibited practices are banned; high-risk systems and GPAI models must meet documentation, transparency, and risk-management obligations before placement on the EU market.
penalties: Fines up to EUR 35M or 7% of worldwide annual turnover (prohibited practices), EUR 15M or 3% (other obligations), per-tier caps.
applicability: Providers, deployers, importers, and distributors of AI systems placing products or services in the EU market.

summary: General Data Protection Regulation: comprehensive data protection law governing processing of personal data of EU data subjects. Key obligations: lawfulness and transparency, purpose limitation, data minimization, data subject rights, breach notification within 72 hours, and DPIA requirements. Applied to AI training pipelines and chatbots processing EU user data.
key_text: paraphrase: personal data must be processed lawfully, fairly, and transparently; data subjects have rights of access, erasure, and objection; controllers must notify breaches within 72 hours.
penalties: Fines up to EUR 20M or 4% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher, for the most serious violations.
applicability: Any controller or processor handling personal data of EU data subjects, wherever established.

summary: Mock statute record: would require annual transparency reports from developers of high-impact AI systems.
key_text: paraphrase: a developer of a high-impact AI system shall publish an annual transparency report to the FTC.
penalties: Fine and civil penalty up to 2% of global turnover.
